newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stock loss at Japan big banks may be 1.7 trln yen.
newsitem.headline: Stock loss at Japan big banks may be 1.7 trln yen.

text.p: Appraisal losses from shareholdings at Japan's top 20 banks are estimated at an aggregate 1.7 trillion yen in the current business year that ended on Monday, Akira Takai, a financial analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd, said.

He told Reuters that he estimated the top 20 banks as a whole had sold shares worth of about three trillion yen in 1996/97, which reduced their aggregate unrealised profits on shareholdings to 6.8 trillion yen at the end of March, 1997. At the end of last September, the unrealised profits at the 20 banks totalled 15.46 trillion yen.

Under Japan's accounting standard, banks must write down appraisal losses on shareholdings if the market value of a share falls below book value. The Nikkei index of 225 leading shares closed the current business year on March 31 at 18,003.40 points, against 21,556.40 at the end of last September and 21,406.85 at the end of 1995/96.

Takai said that the banks would use the stock sales profits to help them write down the appraisal losses and dispose of problem loans. He also said that he expected the 20 banks to dispose of problem loans worth 5.0 trillion to 5.5 trillion yen in 1996/97.
